endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Continuation can coexist with service changes; it is contradicted only by site exit or binding halt.
endpoint_ledger.description: The city maintains the hotel as an active emergency shelter site for displaced families through the dispute period without being forced to vacate the site.
endpoint_ledger.label: continued hotel lease

meta.important_question: Will the city continue using the current hotel lease as the primary emergency shelter site beyond the initial dispute period?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Current dependency structure and lack of named alternative capacity make continuity a strong live option.
realization_criteria: city_housing_department publicly confirms lease continuation or renewal
displaced_families remain housed at the hotel through a later review point
no binding court order requires cessation of current site use
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Corpus explicitly frames continued lease as one endpoint and shows active need supporting continuity at T0.

blockers: provider resistance if alternative is inferior
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Relocation differs from injunction because it can be voluntary, negotiated, or precautionary.
endpoint_ledger.description: Families are moved from the leased hotel to another shelter arrangement or site, whether planned or forced.

meta.important_question: Will displaced families be moved from the hotel to another site because of political, legal, or operational pressure?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Resident pressure and legal uncertainty create a path to site substitution if costs become politically tolerable.

blockers: fact-specific zoning or emergency authority exceptions
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A mere hearing, audit, or delay is not realization unless it creates binding restriction on current use.
endpoint_ledger.description: A court or similar legal authority halts, suspends, or materially restricts use of the hotel for the emergency-housing program.
endpoint_ledger.label: injunction or binding legal restriction

meta.important_question: Will a court or comparable legal process halt or materially restrict the current hotel-based housing arrangement?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Legal process is a major uncertainty lever but not yet realized at T0.
realization_criteria: municipal_court issues injunction, stay, or equivalent binding order against current use

endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario specifically notes courts may review zoning objections, preserving a live legal endpoint.

blockers: political resistance to perceived program entrenchment
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Expansion can coexist with continued lease and is not negated by temporary criticism alone.
endpoint_ledger.description: The city and partners add meaningful onsite services, staffing, or management capacity to stabilize the hotel-based shelter model.
endpoint_ledger.label: service expansion at current site

meta.important_question: Will the city add meaningful onsite services or management capacity rather than only defending the status quo?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Expansion is a mechanism for legitimacy repair and operational stabilization when outright retreat is costly.
realization_criteria: city_housing_department funds or launches new onsite support, management, or safety measures
service_provider_coalition gains expanded formal role at the hotel
publicly documented operational plan increases services beyond baseline shelter provision
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario explicitly includes service expansion as a possible endpoint and provider urgency supports it.

risk_flags.note: Scenario provides only compact summary-level evidence; counts and institutional structure are estimated defaults.
Safety concerns are present as complaints, not confirmed factual findings at T0.
Lack of evidence on substitute shelter inventory creates major uncertainty around relocation feasibility and switching costs.
Court review is possible but schedule, standing, and legal posture are unspecified.
Citywide observers are represented as a population archetype rather than actor, so media exposure to broader public is captured indirectly through sociology rather than actor edge references.

simulation_brief.endpoint_pressure: Terminal choices implied by corpus are continued lease, relocation, injunction, or service expansion.
simulation_brief.summary: A city emergency-housing program is using a leased hotel to house families displaced by fires. Nearby residents raise safety concerns, service providers emphasize urgent shelter need, hotel workers worry about changes to jobs and workplace conditions, and zoning objections may reach court review. Core pressures involve emergency displacement response, neighborhood stigma and legitimacy, operational dependency on the hotel site, and uncertainty over whether the program continues, relocates, is enjoined, or expands services.
time_zero_assumptions: Hotel lease is active or imminently active at T0.
Families displaced by fires need immediate temporary shelter.
Resident complaints are organized enough to matter politically but have not yet fully determined outcome.
Legal review of zoning objections is plausible but unresolved at T0.
Workers face role uncertainty rather than confirmed layoffs or closures at T0.
simulation_brief.title: emergency_housing_hotel_lease_dispute
uncertainty_notes: Exact city size, number of displaced families, lease duration, and hotel ownership structure are not specified.
No named public officials or organizations are provided; civic actors are fictionalized.
Safety concerns are treated as claims and perceptions, not verified incident evidence at T0.

sociology_baseline.note: Residents may update within familiar safety and neighborhood frames but resist far-off humanitarian abstractions.
Visible incidents, court filings, or media spikes could pull ambivalents into opposition.
Conditional supporters and dependent workers are quieter than more oppositional residents.
Neighborhood and professional networks likely sort discussion into resident, provider, and city clusters.
Broader city opinion likely shifts only after repeated cues from media, officials, and court developments.
Local homeowner/resident identity and humanitarian responder identity shape interpretation of the same facts.
Without fresh conflict or rulings, general public attention may fade quickly.
